newsitem.title: UK: Pregnancy doesn't increase osteoporosis risk - study.
newsitem.headline: Pregnancy doesn't increase osteoporosis risk - study.

text.p: Breastfeeding does not have long-term adverse effects on the mineral content of women's bones or increase risks of suffering from the bone-wasting condition osteoporosis, British medical journal The Lancet reported on Friday.

In a research letter two doctors based in Cambridge, England, said they had measured the bone mineral levels of 12 women during breast-feeding, after they had weaned their baby and after the birth of subsequent children.
"Although significant decreases in bone mineral occur during breastfeeding, these changes are reversible and do not persist after a subsequent pregnancy," doctors Ann Laskey and Ann Prentice said.

Some researchers have suggested that the mineral loss suffered by women after childbirth could increase the risk of osteoporosis in later life, particularly in women who conceive again soon after giving birth.

"Extended periods of breastfeeding and closely-spaced pregnancies are unlikely to have a lasting effect on the bone-mineral status and osteoporosis risk of healthy, well-nourished women," the letter said.
